role: Overnight stats card (8 boxes: recording length, sleep, deep sleep, HR range, nadir HR+time, peak HRV+time), overnight HR chart with analysis-window band and clock axis, tags & notes block, peak rolling-RMSSD scan, rolling-window HR nadir, and sleep-stat fallbacks (HealthKit total -> HealthKit boundaries -> recording estimate) for the recovery PDF.
types: OvernightReportRenderer: extension — overnight section drawing and stats
OvernightReportRenderer.OvernightStatValues: struct — what the two stat rows display (HR range optional, peak RMSSD/time optional, recording length, sleep stats)
OvernightReportRenderer.OvernightHRRange: struct — nadir and max HR plus the nadir's clock time (optional)
OvernightReportRenderer.OvernightSleepStats: struct — sleep/deep minutes, formatted strings and labels for row 1
OvernightReportRenderer.PeakRMSSDResult: struct — peak rolling RMSSD and the t_ms of the beat its window is centred on
OvernightReportRenderer.PeakScanWindow: struct — scan window size/step (beats) and optional ms time band
toplevel: File-scope private helpers (formatRecordingDuration, overnightHRSamples, overnightHRY, drawOvernightHRGrid, overnightHRPath, strokeTagPill, storedHRStats, nadirOffset, rollingWindowHRStats, rollingHRSamples, rollingHRWindow, inScanBand) plus five nested value types with synthesized memberwise inits; no globals or persistent state.

units.does: Computes overnight stat values from the RR series, inputs.artifactFlags, session, HealthKit sleep and HealthKit HR. When there are none (100 or fewer beats) returns yPosition with nothing drawn; otherwise draws the 'Overnight Summary' heading, a grey card with two rows of four stat boxes, and returns the y 115pt below the heading.

branches.cond: overnightStatValues returned nil (series has 100 or fewer points)
branches.effect: returns yPosition unchanged, no heading; otherwise draws heading, 100pt card and both rows

units.does: Fills a rounded (r=8) light-grey rectangle at the left margin, y, width x height as the stats card background.

Builds a 'jmm' clock formatter and draws stat row 1 (recording, sleep, deep, HR range) and row 2 (nadir HR + time, peak HRV + time) at boxWidth = contentWidth/4, passing the optional HR range and peak values through.

Returns nil if the series has <=100 points. Otherwise: the peak-HRV search band from peakSearchBand (30-70% of the HealthKit sleep envelope, or of the recording), the peak rolling RMSSD in it (nil when none measurable) with its clock time from series.wallClockTime; the HR range and nadir time from overnightHRRange (nil when no HR); the recording length as first-to-last beat on the wall clock (gaps included); and sleep stats from computeOvernightSleepStats with the t_ms-based recording minutes (the same input the Overnight screen's estimate uses). Packs them into OvernightStatValues.

branches.effect: false: returns nil (section draws nothing); true: computes stats
peakRMSSD and peakHRVTime are nil (boxes print as missing); otherwise the peak and its wall-clock time

units.does: Draws row 1 of the overnight card: Recording (formatted length), the sleep box (label/value from OvernightSleepStats), the deep-sleep box, and HR Range as 'min-max' in whole bpm, or the missing-value dash when hrRange is nil.

The peak-HRV search band in the series' t_ms: the 30-70% slice of the HealthKit sleep envelope (sleepStart/sleepEnd as ms after sessionStart, clamped to 0...recording length) when both boundaries exist, else of the whole recording (0...last-first t_ms). Mirrors OvernightChartsView.searchBand so the PDF and the Overnight screen search the same stretch. An envelope ending before it starts gives an inverted (empty) band.

branches.cond: sleepData has both sleepStart and sleepEnd
branches.effect: band is within the sleep envelope; otherwise within the whole recording

units.does: Peak rolling RMSSD (300-beat window, 30-beat step) whose window centre falls inside the given t_ms band; if none qualifies, rescans the whole recording. Returns the peak and the t_ms of its centre beat, or nil when points are empty or no window anywhere had a measurable RMSSD (so the report prints a missing value, not 0 ms).

branches.effect: returns nil

branches.cond: no peak found in the band
branches.effect: scans the whole recording
